sections.content:
14,530 people

were counted on the census as "biological scientists" in England and Wales in March 2021.
Biological scientists examine and investigate the morphology, structure, and physical characteristics of living organisms, including their inter-relationships, environments and diseases.

People who had this job were generally similar in age to the working population

The occupation of "biological scientists" had a similar age profile compared with the whole working population.

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 25 to 29 years. Of the whole working population 11.1% were aged 25 to 29 years. For people working as "biological scientists", 12.9% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "biological scientists" was 16 to 19 years.

sections.title: The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 25 to 29 years
sections.footer: Source: Census 2021 from Office for National Statistics

sections.content:
Other jobs that had a similar age profile to "biological scientists" included:

  • publicans and managers of licensed premises
  • TV, video and audio servicers and repairers
  • authors, writers and translators

Select your age group to see the ten most popular occupations for your age

More men than women had this job

Among people working as "biological scientists" there were more men than women (56% compared with 44%).

This means "biological scientists" had a different proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "science, research, engineering and technology professionals".

Men made up 56% and women made up 44% of "biological scientists"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women. This occupation was one of the jobs for which the proportion of men and women was closest to this overall picture.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "biological scientists" included:

  • betting shop and gambling establishment managers
  • paramedics
  • restaurant and catering establishment managers and proprietors

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

We can look at who worked as "biological scientists" by age group and for men and women at the same time to see how these two factors interact.

Among those aged 50 years and older, we see there is a higher proportion of men with this occupation than women.

The percentage of men and women who are "biological scientists" across age groups

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "biological scientists", 9.7% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had a similar age profile compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work full-time than part-time (79.9% compared with 20.1%).

They are also more likely to be an employee (81.8%) than self-employed (18.2%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was the South East. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Wiltshire, this is in the region of the South West.
